clue.text: Writers on law are, sir, just in a way

indicators.note: in a way suggests the letters of sir and just are arranged in some other fashion

explanation.surface: A remark that legal writers really are, sir, fair-minded after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges SIR and JUST; 'are' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jurists are experts in law, especially those who write learned commentary on it.

clue.text: More perfect societies

parts.note: reads as better communities, but More is Sir Thomas More, whose ideal island commonwealth gave its name to every imagined perfect state

explanation.definitionFit: Ideal imaginary commonwealths are named after Thomas More's book about a perfect island state.

clue.text: Your old place in terrible dim bar suggests hymn to Bacchus

indicators.note: in places the archaic possessive within the reworked letters of the bar
terrible says the letters of dim bar are mangled into a new order

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An archaic home inside a dingy pub conjures up an ode to the wine god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DIM BAR into DIRAMB, and 'in' puts THY inside it; 'suggests' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb was a wild choral song in honour of the wine god Dionysus, the Greek Bacchus.

clue.text: Echo, for example, New York speed measurement

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: Asking whether Echo might be a New York unit of velocity.
explanation.walkthrough: Echo is the mountain spirit of Greek myth who pined for Narcissus.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo was a nymph in Greek mythology, a minor female nature spirit.

clue.text: Its cohorts were gleaming in purple and gold

definitions.text: Its cohorts were gleaming in purple and gold

parts.words: Its cohorts were gleaming in purple and gold
parts.note: a line from Byron's The Destruction of Sennacherib, describing the army of the ancient empire that came down like the wolf on the fold

explanation.walkthrough: Byron's poem opens: 'The Assyrian came down like the wolf on the fold, / And his cohorts were gleaming in purple and gold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's poem describes the soldiers of the ancient Mesopotamian empire of Sennacherib in those colours.

clue.text: Secret of Wilkie Collins

parts.note: the words preceding Secret in the title of a Wilkie Collins novel of 1857

explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie Collins wrote a novel titled with these words followed by Secret, so they complete his title.

clue.text: Surtees's comedian annoyed?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Surtees's funny man has lost his temper.

explanation.definitionFit: Surtees's novel about the hunting grocer Jorrocks bears this title, the name of a fictional town.

clue.text: Tolstoy revival

explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's last novel bears this title, and the word means rising again or coming back to life.

clue.text: Fate of Susan Ferrier

clue.text: Part-time typist (English) in Greek vale

explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe is a famous gorge in Thessaly, praised by ancient poets.

clue.text: They're unbeatable when skinless

explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe, Elizabethan dramatist, was killed in a tavern brawl at Deptford in 1593.
